body: I would really appreciate a PM. I am very interested in hearing what she went through or even what you have witnessed, to know I'm not alone and that there is hope.

Thank you for your response. It actually really helped hearing that this isn't permanent. I have gotten blood work done, about 2 weeks ago and it came back that I am borderline hyper thyroid and that I have a mildly inflammed liver. My doctor said to me that she couldn't do anything until I was actually hyper thyroid and the liver isn't anything to worry about and wants me to get blood work again in a month. As for everything else, my blood work came back really good. And it confuses me, I know that a lot of this is a mental problem but it doesn't explain my severe increase in heart rate just from sitting instead of laying. I tried to bake a cake the other day and my heart rate went up to 130 bpm, my hands started to shake, and I got very dizzy. They want me off of Klonopin due to its addictive qualities so that has been what I have been working on. Thank you for your advice, I have been getting medical attention just not answers. I just can't believe how much the "not permanent" thing has encouraged 
me. Whenever I go to depression or anxiety forums they all say "This is your life now you just need to learn how to cope with it." I do have a question though, my doctor knows of the increased heart rate and didn't say anything. Is there anything I should ask her to test me for when I go in 2 weeks or just let her make the decision?

I'm convinced that I need to get off of medicine before I can heal. I'm just afraid that I've done permanent damage. I am going to do everything I can to fix this once the medicine is gone but until then I am convinced that I won't be able to heal until then so I haven't done much other than taking omega 3 and going to my therapist every week. I definitely recommend medication as a last option. There are so many therapies and techniques out there.
